description: Gelcha Kindu is our coffee station in Gedeb, Ethiopia, located at 2,361 m.a.s.l. We produce experimental 74110 coffees using innovative processing methods to achieve exceptional quality. A portion of this auction's proceeds will support the expansion of a local school and improve educational opportunities for children in the community.
fermentationDetails: Four Layer High Fermentation: The coffee undergoes a 48–52-hour first stage fermentation in sealed plastic bags, followed by thick layer shade drying on raised beds to develop distinctive flavors and quality.

description: Muje Mesina Station was established at Guji in 2015 at an altitude of 2010 m.a.s.l. The station produces coffee varieties 74110, 74112, and 74165 and was among the first stations to introduce fermentation processing. Its fermented coffee won the 2018 World Barista Champion, and coffees from the station have continued to win numerous competitions.
fermentationDetails: Two Layer Fermentation: The coffee undergoes a 24-30 hour first stage fermentation in sealed plastic bags, followed by thick layer shade drying on raised beds to develop distinctive flavors and quality.

description: Muje Mesina Station was established in at Guji 2015 at an altitude of 2010 m.a.s.l. fermentationDetails: Our lot is processed using our proprietary Anaris Fermentation method, a controlled anaerobic fermentation process carried out in brewery grade stainless-steel tanks. Nitrogen is injected every six hours to maintain an oxygen free environment and promote consistent fermentation.

description: Owned by Mr. Abreham Mengister, Koke Shalye Station is located in Koke Kebele at 1,973 m.a.s.l. Shalye means “beautiful” in the local language. The station produces rare 74110, 74112, and 74165 coffees using pure spring water. Its coffees have earned recognition and awards in competitions at various levels.
fermentationDetails: Three Layer Medium Fermentation: The coffee undergoes a 32-38 hour first stage fermentation in sealed plastic bags, followed by thick layer shade drying on raised beds to develop distinctive flavors and quality.

description: Amederaro is our second washing station, located in Yirgacheffee Konga Wete at 2099 m.a.s.l. The station produces 74110, 74112 & 74166 variety coffee and specializes in experimental lots, many of which have achieved success in coffee competitions. In the local language, Amederaro means "let us bloom." Through the proceeds from this auction, we support a neighboring school and provide electricity to local farming communities.
fermentationDetails: We call this process Mustica Fermentation. In this method, mosto yeast is prepared from coffee that has undergone anaerobic fermentation. It is diluted with clean water and adjusted to a pH of 4 before being mixed with freshly harvested coffee to initiate fermentation.

fermentationDetails: We call it Riverlock Fermentation. Red coffee cherries are sealed in oxygen free bags and submerged in a river, where the cold, flowing water supports a long, slow fermentation. This process contributes to a distinctive cup profile.

description: Gargari Gutity is our own coffee station in Gutity, Gedeb, Ethiopia, at 2,349 m.a.s.l. We produce washed and experimental coffees from the 74110 variety, using water from the Gutity River. “Gargari Mene” means uniting and looking out for one another. In 2026, our coffee achieved first place in the Taste of Harvest competition.
fermentationDetails: The coffee undergoes anaerobic fermentation in a stainless-steel tank for 72 hours. It is then pulped without water and rested for 6 hours before a second sealed anaerobic fermentation for 116 hours. Finally, it is dried on raised African beds under shade.

fermentationDetails: This process combines two fermentation methods. First, the coffee cherries are partially dried on African drying beds until they lose more than 50% of their moisture. The dried cherries then undergo a skin-loosening process before being pulped. Finally, the coffee is dried again to achieve the desired moisture content.
